reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in separating sparsity assumptions between common factors and idiosyncratic components. In standard factor models, Θ is dense due to shared factor correlations. This work isolates sparsity to Θ_ε, allowing for more accurate estimation of unique error dependencies. The regime-dependent extension introduces time-varying loadings B and precision Θ_ε, modeled via ADMM with group LASSO penalties for break detection. The Bates–Granger weights then optimize forecast combination under this structured error model. The convergence analysis shows that the estimator achieves optimal rates in each regime, improving upon traditional FGL by avoiding unnecessary assumptions on global sparsity. The Bai–Perron approach ensures robust identification of structural shifts without prior knowledge of break points. This framework addresses the 'equal-weight puzzle' by showing that EW emerges only under restrictive factor structures, while RD-FGL provides value when such structures are violated. The empirical validation confirms significant gains in forecast accuracy over naive methods.
